You are the Kalshi Edge Hunter. This cycle is CREATIVE, not a scorecard audit.

Hard rule: Do NOT just re-rank cells that /api/scorecard already shows as positive. The owner already knows NY HIGH/LOW mid and Seattle/Phoenix HIGH mid look good on paper. Your job is to invent strategy, calibration, and structure ideas that the current logging and cell system do not already measure.

Prior context (do not re-discover):
- NY daily HIGH mid ~+15c, LOW mid ~+24c on small n; Seattle/Phoenix HIGH mid mildly positive.
- Hourly far-strike D3 NO looked like a fee-surviving edge earlier.
- Overall would_bet still slightly negative; D1 mid-strike hourly is systematically broken.
- Evidence had a temporary API lag; ensembles resume soon.
- Daily half-spread ~1.6c; much of the NO loss is execution cost.

You MAY pull live data to ground ideas:
- https://kalshiml-production.up.railway.app/api/state
- /api/scorecard
- /api/gap_diag
- /api/spread_decomp
- /api/cell?cell=... (only if needed to test a NEW idea)
- /api/ml/status
- /api for catalog

What to produce:
Propose 4–7 DISTINCT ideas across these categories (cover at least 3 categories):

A. Probability calibration
   - shrinkage / isotonic / city-specific / lead-time-dependent / ensemble-disagreement gates
   - how current p_yes is mis-used at extremes

B. Ladder / structure betting
   - multi-strike packages, progressive NO ladders, mid-vs-cheap coupling, relative-value across strikes
   - how to size and exit a ladder as a single position

C. Execution & microstructure
   - maker-only, avoid one-sided books, size by confidence band, join-bid vs cross

D. Regime / filter ideas the current cells miss
   - weather setup types, model-run age interactions, cross-city relative value, formation dynamics

E. New logging or measurement the system should add so these ideas become testable

For EACH idea write:
1. Title
2. Why it could be +EV (mechanism, not vibes)
3. How to test it with EXISTING data (which endpoints / fields) OR what new logging is required
4. Rough priority (high / med / low) and a concrete next experiment

Then append 4–7 findings lines to agents/kalshi-edge-hunter/findings.jsonl (read file first, append, github_commit). Use type: action_proposal or edge_hypothesis. Be specific.

Also write_memory with a short creative-cycle summary.

Final answer: ranked list of the best NEW ideas only (no rehash of known NY mid cells). Max 22 turns. Think freely; cost is not the bottleneck.
result.final_answer:
## Creative Cycle — Ranked NEW Ideas

*(Note: this environment has no HTTP tool, so I grounded ideas in prior logged findings rather than live pulls. Findings appended to `findings.jsonl`, memory written.)*

### 1. [E — HIGH] Richer decision logging: book context, ladder prices, ensemble_std, forecast_age, counterfactual PnL
**Mechanism:** Every structural idea below is currently untestable because evidence records lack bid/ask+depth, full strike ladder at decision time, ensemble member spread, model-run timestamp, and maker-vs-taker counterfactual PnL. A few KB per decision makes every future idea measurable without scorer changes.
**Test:** PR the recorder fields; value accrues from next decision. **Priority: HIGH — highest-leverage single change.**

### 2. [B — HIGH] Progressive far-strike NO ladder as ONE package
**Mechanism:** Known D3 far-strike NO edge dies by variance (one 97c loss erases ~9 wins at 2c). But exactly one strike settles YES per event — buying NO across all k qualifying far strikes is anti-correlated by construction. Cost ≈ 2k cents, payoff ≈ 100(k−1). Converts "is this cell right" into "did the outcome land in our covered tail at all," a much lower-variance bet on tail mass.
**Test:** Offline sim grouping historical would_bet far-strike decisions by event_ticker; compare package Sharpe vs per-cell. **Priority: HIGH.**

### 3. [C — MED-HIGH] Maker-only execution band when edge < 4c
**Mechanism:** Half-spread ~1.6c + 1452/4071 one-sided books means crossing eats >50% of a 3c edge. Join-bid keeps ~3c vs ~1.4c; adverse selection on one-sided books is worse than fill-rate loss.
**Test:** Re-score would_bet with entry=bid for two-sided books; add "hypothetical maker PnL" as standard scorecard column. **Priority: MED-HIGH.**

### 4. [A — MED] Ensemble-disagreement sizing gate
**Mechanism:** A 55% with 2% inter-model spread ≠ 55% with 12% spread. Disagreement = regime novelty where shrinkage fails; market mid partially prices width, our point estimate doesn't. Expect low-std tercile ~0/positive, high-std deeply negative.
**Test:** Bin would_bet PnL by ensemble_std tercile (needs logging from idea #1 if not present). **Priority: MED.**

### 5. [D — MED] Forecast-age interaction explains broken D1 hourly
**Mechanism:** D1 mid-strike predicted 33–38% vs actual 11–18% — maybe the bug isn't the strike bucket but stale model runs; the market updates within minutes, our model only at run boundaries.
**Test:** Bin PnL by forecast_age_min (<2h/2–6h/>6h); expect monotone decay. Needs run timestamp logging. **Priority: MED.**

### 6. [D — LOW-MED] Cross-city relative value on daily HIGH buckets
**Mechanism:** NY (+16c) vs Seattle/Phoenix (mild) suggests attention/liquidity-driven pricing quality differs. When two cities show similar ensemble distributions but different prices (base-rate adjusted), buy cheap/sell rich. Invisible to per-city cells.
**Test:** Per-city mean(model_p − market_p) on daily HIGH mid from evidence logs. **Priority: LOW-MED.**

All 6 committed to `agents/kalshi-edge-hunter/findings.jsonl` (sha ad52cca) as action_proposal/edge_hypothesis lines; memory summary written.
